tool: Nsight Compute, HPC SDK 26.3, section SpeedOfLight
question: The same ladder term appeared to run at ~74% of FP64 peak synthetically and ~14% in molecular CCSD. Proposed cause: the second step reshapes to M=v^2, N=o^2, K=v^2, so o^2 is the short dimension and frozen-core molecular runs have small o. This holds v fixed at 300 and varies only o.
verdict: REFUTED. Kernel efficiency is ~98% of compute roofline in BOTH regimes and BOTH backends. The grid does shrink 5x with o^2, so the GEMM is smaller, but it is not less efficient.
what_this_means: Combined with nsys (job 161307), which found kernels occupy ~3% of wall time at 240 AO: the GPU performs its arithmetic at essentially the hardware limit and then waits. The earlier 'efficiency' figures divided a derived FLOP count by GPU SECTION time, and section time is overwhelmingly allocation, pinning, transfer and Python rather than kernels -- so those figures were never kernel efficiencies. Every remaining opportunity in this code path is host-side, which is also why FP64 emulation returned 1.15x where the microbenchmark promised 2.90x, and why fixing host pinning returns 37%.
aside: Low occupancy (12-25%) is normal for FP64 tensor-core GEMMs, which are register- and shared-memory-limited per block. ncu's 'Est. Local Speedup' occupancy advice should not be read as headroom when SM throughput is already 98%.
kernels: cutlass_80_tensorop_d884gemm_* -- sm_80 (Ampere) DMMA kernels. Identical set and efficiency in both backends.
